reasoning: Combined the overlapping double-definition guidance into one sharper rule and kept completion/partial-name specificity separate to avoid redundancy. Preserved the distinct acronym-expansion, bare-prompt relation, and temporal eligibility checks. Support counts reflect how many of the two source patches support each edit; no edits target the protected section. [optimizer-ranked: selected 3/5 edits]

edits.target: - In trivia or wordplay clues, treat a parenthetical number as a hard answer-length constraint. For a double-definition clue (for example, “X, or what Y is put to”), seek the exact word that fits both senses rather than a synonym that fits only one. Use any proper-name cue to identify the requested name or name part.
edits.content: - In trivia or wordplay clues, treat a parenthetical number as a hard answer-length constraint. For double- or multi-definition clues (for example, “X, or what Y is put to”), seek the exact lexical headword that fits every independent sense and any corroborating context hint, rather than a synonym that fits only one sense or a modifier or fragment from the clue. Use any proper-name cue to identify the requested name or name part.

edits.target: - Treat terse statements, quoted fragments, and incomplete phrases as information-seeking clues when appropriate. Infer the answer slot from the wording, then use the context to identify the entity or value that satisfies the clue.
edits.content: - For a bare place name, list of people, or slogan or catchphrase, do not automatically echo the input or select a nearby title based only on matching words. Use context to infer a salient associated relation—such as a place's country, a shared work for performers or characters, or the source work or franchise for a catchphrase—and answer with that relation only when clearly supported. If a quoted catchphrase also appears in a derivative work's title, distinguish the phrase's source from that title; if the intended relation remains ambiguous, do not guess.

edits.target: - For a Spoonerism clue, identify the swapped sounds and restore them to recover the intended expression. Return that expression rather than the person or entity it refers to, unless the question explicitly asks for that entity.
edits.content: - When a clue gives an acronym or initialism and asks what feature or name it indicates, return its conventional expansion. Do not substitute an associated mechanism, device, or implementation detail.

ranking_details.reasoning: Edit 0 has the strongest support and sharpens an existing rule for exact multi-sense answers. Edit 2 fills a broader gap around inferring relations from bare prompts while guarding against unsupported guesses. Edit 1 adds a distinct answer-slot check for acronym expansions. Edit 3 largely repeats existing granularity guidance, and edit 4 is a narrower comparison refinement.
